sec: Addisonian crisis, 1° vs 2° table and diagnostic tests · p850

items.q: The listed causes of weakness, fatigue and weight loss include TB, HIV, malignancy, lymphoma and:
items.exp: Note: causes of weakness, fatigue & weight loss — TB, HIV, malignancy, lymphoma, Addison's disease. (Book p850)

opts: Infection (any stress) and abrupt steroid withdrawal
items.exp: Precipitated by infection (any stress) and abrupt steroid withdrawal. (Book p850)

items.q: Features of Addisonian crisis include acute abdominal pain, vomiting, constipation, hypoglycaemia and:
items.exp: Crisis features: acute abdominal pain, vomiting, constipation, hypoglycaemia, hypotension/circulatory failure; Rx fluids + steroids. (Book p850)

items.q: Match 1° vs 2° adrenal insufficiency — 1) MC axis  2) ACTH  3) Hyperpigmentation … A) ↑ in 1°, ↓ in 2°  B) ↓ in 1°, normal (ACTH-independent) in 2°  C) + in 1°, − in 2°
items.exp: MC is ↓ in 1° but normal (ACTH independent) in 2°; ACTH ↑ in 1°, ↓ in 2°; hyperpigmentation + in 1°, − in 2°. (Book p850)

items.q: ‘Serum sodium falls in BOTH primary and secondary adrenal insufficiency.’
opts: False — sodium is normal in both
items.exp: S. sodium ↓↓ in both; S. potassium ↑ only in 1° (normal in 2°). (Book p850)

items.q: Which pair of findings is present in 1° but ABSENT in 2° insufficiency?
opts: Loss of axillary hair and ↓ sodium
items.exp: Salt craving/postural hypotension (+/−) and hyperpigmentation (+/−) distinguish 1° from 2°; axillary hair loss is ++ vs +. (Book p850)

items.q: A fasting cortisol below what value diagnoses Addison's disease directly?
items.exp: Fasting cortisol <3 µg/dL = Addison's; >20 µg/dL rules it out; 3–20 needs the Synacthen test. (Book p850)

items.q: A fasting cortisol above what value rules out Addison's?

opts: 250 µg IM or IV synacthen/cosyntropin/synthetic ACTH
items.exp: Inject 250 µg IM/IV synacthen (cosyntropin/synthetic ACTH); measure cortisol at 30 and 60 min (consider highest value). (Book p850)

items.q: On the ACTH stimulation test, a peak cortisol below what value confirms Addison's?
items.exp: <18 µg/dL confirms Addison's; >18 µg/dL rules it out. (Book p850)
